title: flacmn deck pro housing
purpose: Housing for the flacmn deck pro hi-fi shelf music player: Raspberry Pi 4 + DAC Pro stack, a small screen and two encoder knobs, line out at the rear.
_comment: Stage 0 of /design. options: how many designs to draw per round; 1 unless the owner asks for options. requirements: {id, text, priority must|should|free, provenance given|measured|chosen|estimated, source, check {lhs, op, rhs} (optional, over option parameters and bbox_x/y/z, parts_total, parts_make, parts_buy, fasteners, setups)}. Keys starting with _ are notes. See .claude/skills/design/references/schemas.md.

defaults.printed: PETG, FDM (brief: PETG or ASA near the Pi; PLA softens at 55-60 C)

requirements.text: Holds a Raspberry Pi 4 B with the DAC Pro on 9 mm standoffs above it (stack ~85 x 56 x 35) on 4 M2.5 posts, 58 x 49 pattern
Front face: 5in screen on the left; a large knob (~57) and a small knob (~35) to its right, as in flacmn_deck_layout.svg
No knob on the side faces (both knobs on the front)
Rear face: the inputs and outputs (the plan leaves the rear layout to the designer)
Use the boards' own sockets; add panel-mount extensions only where a socket cannot reach the rear
Openings: power USB-C, 2 x RCA line out, Ethernet, 4 x USB-A (music drive in one); headphone jack and status LED optional
No openings for HDMI or a power button
microSD stays in the Pi's slot; reachable through a wall slot or an easy-to-remove lid
Sheds 8-10 W with no fan; under ~70 C after 30 min of converting (thermal pad to aluminium, or heatsink + 10-15 cm2 vents low and high)
Wi-Fi gets out (plastic housing, or a plastic window over the antenna, or Ethernet only)
Encoder walls thin enough for the M7 nut to catch on the 7 mm bushing (wall <= ~4 at the knobs)
Knob caps ~57 and ~35 diameter, 13 thick, 1 mm proud of the front face on the 15 mm encoder shafts (shaft tip at the cap face)
RCA and headphone leads short and away from the USB-C power lead
Rubber feet: stands still and air passes underneath
Fewest parts and fastenings that do all of the above
Wall thickness, flange size, screw positions, exact sizes within the layout
Screen: Waveshare 5inch DSI LCD (lens 120.7 x 77.2, VA 109 x 65.8, 13 deep), DSI ribbon to the Pi; held by VHB
Power USB-C, 2 x RCA and headphone jack out the back panel on the boards' own sockets; USB and Ethernet cords plug into the Pi inside and thread out through cut-outs in the back panel
Hand-folded aluminium sheet; processor heat to the aluminium through a thermal pad, no vents
Wi-Fi: a plastic window over the Pi's antenna, or Ethernet only
No balanced-out openings or reserved room
Nothing protrudes except the knob caps, the M3 socket-head screw heads and the feet
As few screws as possible

Construction: one folded shell (front face in the centre; top, floor and sides fold back) with folded tabs at the back of the top and floor; a flat, unbent back plate fixed by 4 M3 screws entering from the back face into the tabs
Fasteners: conventional hex-socket screws from the library: ISO 4762 M3 x 8 socket head (projects/grindmn_screw_m3x8)
requirements.source: owner, 2026-11-11 (round 5: flacmn_deck_layout.svg + answers); the owner's 'vault' read as this repo's screw part

requirements.text: Rear plate removable: take it off, plug the cords in, thread them through its cut-outs, refit it
Envelope ~241 W x 88.5 H x 100.5 D (owner's layout at true scale; the pasted electronics were at 0.847)
Pi 4 + DAC Pro flat on the floor at the back right; USB/Ethernet ports face the free space behind the screen

bought_parts.name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B
bought_parts._note: no model yet; build from the Raspberry Pi mechanical drawing

bought_parts.name: Bourns PEC11R-4215F-S0024 x 2 (15 mm shaft)
bought_parts._note: owner 2026-11-11: 15 mm shafts, so the shaft ends inside the 10.5 mm caps

conflicts.text: No face takes every socket without an add-on: USB-C power, the DAC Pro RCA and headphone sockets are on the Pi's long side; USB and Ethernet are on its short edge. Either the USB/Ethernet edge goes to a side wall, or the rear needs a USB-C extension plus RCA/jack panel sockets wired to the DAC headers.
conflicts.resolution: owner: power, RCA and headphones out the rear on their own sockets; USB x4 and Ethernet out the left side; no add-ons (2026-11-11)

conflicts.text: 3.5in HDMI screen: the Pi 4's two micro-HDMI sockets are on the same long side as USB-C, directly under the DAC Pro's RCA sockets. A cable plug there (25-35 mm with its bend, ~10 even with a flat FPC adapter) stops that side from reaching the rear wall, so with the 3.5in screen the RCA and power cannot use their own sockets at the rear. The 2in SPI screen (jumpers to the GPIO) has no such cable.
conflicts.resolution: owner: size for the 2in SPI screen now; no HDMI (2026-11-11)

conflicts.text: Pi 4 microSD is on the short edge opposite USB/Ethernet. If USB/Ethernet faces the left wall, the SD edge faces the right wall, where the side knob is; a wall slot only works if the Pi spans wall to wall, otherwise the base must come off.
conflicts.resolution: designer: follows from the layout; solved in the round (wall slot if the Pi spans wall to wall, else removable base)

conflicts.text: Housing_Plan.pdf is an arrangement, not to scale: the knob circles are drawn ~3/4 of the face height, a 25 mm knob is far smaller. Positions are taken from it; sizes from the parts.
conflicts.resolution: designer: arrangement from the plan, sizes from the parts (2026-11-11)

conflicts.text: Flush knobs: a 2 mm rim (knob = height - 4, chosen 2026-11-11) leaves ~0.3-1.2 mm of 1 mm sheet above and below the knob opening, next to the folds. Hand-folded 1 mm sheet needs ~3.5 mm: knob = height - 7.

open_questions.question: Screen: 2in SPI or 3.5in HDMI (owner decides after testing the 2in)
Stack height with the DAC Pro: measure
Confirm the DAC Pro RCA/jack face the Pi's USB-C long side
Pi 4 Wi-Fi antenna position (for a metal housing)
Balanced out: openings now or room for later
Knob caps: bought or machined (57 x 10.5 with a counterbore over the nut)

notes.text: I want the buttons to only be 5mm  thck and I want their diameter to be equal to the height of the deck, otherwise move forward with the design
I want the buttons flush to the surface of the volume and i don't want anthing protruding
owner (gap answers to the flush push-back): knob = height - 4; feet on the underside are fine. Also: I also want as few screws as possible
the cutout doesn't need to surround the whole dial. Have a small cutout for the encoder and the button will slide over the protruding encoder
restart the design from this base (flacmn_deck_layout.svg, commit e22ecdf)

I no longer want the front to mount separately. I want the bent portion to be made up of the front face in the center, and the sides, top and bottom bending backwards. Then I want the rear plate to mount to the rear using m3
I want there to be 4 m3 screws to enter from the back face and I want the back plate to have no bending, add folded tabs to the top and bottom pieces
designer correction after build: the folded tabs put the nuts 0.5 mm nearer the top and floor than the back plate's screw holes; move the holes to match (owner approved round 7: 'Approved, build it')
Make caps 13 mm thick (so the 15 mm PEC11R-4215F shaft ends at the cap face)

_designer_notes: Round 3: heat goes from the Pi underside through a 3 mm pad into the base plate, which is the exposed underside between the feet.
Round 3: Wi-Fi window is a 35 x 6 slot in the base plate under the Pi's antenna corner; Ethernet is the fallback.
Round 3: microSD is reached by removing the 2 base screws and lowering the plate.
Every fold uses an UNTESTED slot recipe; coupons before cutting.
